purpose: Explain why checkpoint batching was selected, how it changed replay behavior, and what must be validated before paging is enabled.

sections.title: The problem to solve
sections.summary: A 50,000-record replay exceeded the operations window at the recorded 18-minute baseline.

sections.title: Decision and implementation
sections.summary: Bounded checkpoint batches were selected and merged with focused tests and benchmark checks.

sections.title: Measured result
sections.summary: The recorded replay completed in 6 minutes, a 12-minute reduction from baseline.

sections.title: Operational implications
sections.summary: Replay-safe staging preserves comparison quality, while alert thresholds remain the next validation boundary.

claims.statement: The recorded 50,000-record replay took 18 minutes and exceeded the operations window.
claims.implication: Replay duration was an operational constraint, not a cosmetic performance concern.

claims.statement: The implementation uses bounded checkpoint batches during replay.
claims.implication: Bounded batches reduce replay time while retaining explicit progress checkpoints.

claims.statement: The checkpoint implementation merged with focused tests and successful benchmark checks.
claims.implication: The reported outcome includes reviewed implementation and recorded validation, not activity alone.

claims.statement: Checkpoint batching reduced the recorded replay from 18 minutes to 6 minutes.
claims.implication: The 12-minute reduction brings the synthetic replay back inside the stated operations window.

claims.statement: Staging load tests use replay-safe mode so duplicate callbacks do not invalidate comparisons.
claims.implication: The operating constraint explains why the before-and-after benchmark remains comparable.

claims.statement: Alert thresholds must be validated against replay spikes before paging is enabled.
claims.implication: Threshold validation prevents synthetic replay behavior from creating noisy operational alerts.
